skill.name: kegg-database
skill.description: Access KEGG REST data for academic bioinformatics research, including pathways, genes, compounds, drugs, ID conversion, and interaction lookups.
skill.summary: Query KEGG REST data for pathway, gene, compound, drug, and identifier mapping workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The confirmed risk is intentional outbound KEGG REST traffic from scripts/kegg_api.py. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, biological identifiers, HTTP status documentation, and examples. No evidence found for prompt injection, malicious exfiltration intent, filesystem access, or command execution.

remediation.issue: Outbound KEGG requests are made without explicit timeout settings.
remediation.suggestion: Add timeout values to every urllib.request.urlopen call and document that queries leave the local environment.

remediation.issue: Some KEGG URL path components are built directly from function arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Validate database names, organism codes, entry IDs, and options before constructing REST paths.

remediation.issue: Drug interaction lookups may be mistaken for clinical guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear wording that KEGG DDI output is for research and not medical decision-making.

content.user_title: Query KEGG Pathways and Gene Data
content.value_statement: Bioinformatics researchers need reliable KEGG lookups for pathways, genes, compounds, and drugs. This skill provides direct KEGG REST helpers and reference guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Fetch KEGG database metadata with kegg_info.
List KEGG pathways, genes, compounds, enzymes, diseases, and drugs.
Search KEGG records by keyword, formula, exact mass, or molecular weight.
Retrieve KEGG entries, sequences, structures, images, KGML, and pathway JSON.
Convert identifiers between KEGG, NCBI, UniProt, PubChem, and ChEBI.
Find cross-references and drug-drug interactions through KEGG REST endpoints.
limitations: KEGG REST access is for academic users and academic use only.
The helper returns raw KEGG response text that still needs parsing.
External network access to rest.kegg.jp is required for live results.
KEGG limits most batch requests to 10 entries, with stricter limits for images and JSON.

use_cases.title: Map Genes to Pathways
use_cases.description: Find KEGG pathways linked to human, mouse, yeast, or bacterial genes for research analysis.

use_cases.title: Prepare Identifier Crosswalks
use_cases.description: Convert KEGG gene or compound IDs to NCBI, UniProt, PubChem, or ChEBI identifiers.

use_cases.title: Review Drug Interaction Records
use_cases.description: Query KEGG drug-drug interaction records for pharmacology research and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up a Pathway
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the KEGG entry for human glycolysis. Summarize the pathway name, organism scope, and any important lookup limits.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Gene to Pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: Use KEGG to find pathways linked to human TP53. Return pathway identifiers, names, and a short research summary.

prompt_templates.title: Convert External Identifiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert hsa:10458 from KEGG to UniProt and NCBI Gene IDs. Note any missing mappings or ambiguous results.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Organism Pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare glycolysis pathway records for human, mouse, and yeast in KEGG. Respect KEGG batch limits and summarize key differences.

output_examples.input: Find KEGG pathways for TP53 in humans.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the human TP53 gene entry, lists linked KEGG pathways, and summarizes pathway names returned by KEGG.

output_examples.input: Convert hsa:10458 to UniProt and NCBI identifiers.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes each target database mapping, reports matched identifiers, and notes any missing KEGG conversion results.

output_examples.input: Check KEGG drug interactions for D00001 and D00002.
output_examples.output: The response reports documented KEGG interaction records, explains empty results, and avoids clinical advice.

best_practices: Confirm that your use complies with KEGG academic-use terms before querying.
Batch no more than 10 entries per KEGG request.
Cache repeated research lookups to reduce unnecessary API traffic.
anti_patterns: Do not use KEGG REST output as medical or clinical advice.
Do not run rapid repeated requests against KEGG endpoints.
Do not assume raw KEGG text is already normalized for downstream analysis.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps query KEGG REST endpoints for academic bioinformatics research workflows.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. Live results require outbound HTTPS requests to rest.kegg.jp.

faq.question: Can it be used for commercial work?
faq.answer: The skill notes that KEGG API access is for academic users and academic use only.

faq.question: What data types can it retrieve?
faq.answer: It can retrieve entries, pathway links, sequences, compound structures, images, KGML, and pathway JSON when KEGG supports them.

faq.question: Does it parse results automatically?
faq.answer: No. The helper functions return raw KEGG response text for the user or workflow to parse.

faq.question: Can it check drug interactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can query KEGG DDI records for research, but it should not be used for clinical decisions.
